value: wild western fence lizards fled at longer distances from an approaching person wearing a red T-shirt than a dark blue one (p = 0.033, Cohen's d = 0.83); T-shirt colour affected flight initiation distance (F = 2.89, p = 0.039)
units: categorical (flight initiation distance by observer T-shirt colour; F test, post hoc p corrected for multiple comparisons)

source.authors: Breanna J. Putman, Jonathan P. Drury, Daniel T. Blumstein, Gregory B. Pauly
source.title: Fear no colors? Observer clothing color influences lizard escape behavior

method: behavioural: field flight-initiation-distance trials, one person approaching wild lizards in a T-shirt of one of four colours (dark blue, light blue, grey, red)
conditions: Wild lizards at two Southern California sites, Griffith Park (heavily used public park) and Stunt Ranch (restricted reserve). 114 trials in all: 15 dark blue, 14 light blue, 15 grey, 15 red at Griffith Park and 14, 14, 13, 14 at Stunt Ranch; the Results do not give the number of individual lizards, and repeat trials on one individual were avoided by walking in one direction and not sampling a location twice. Shirts were worn in random order and the colour changed every 3 to 4 trials per day. Dark and light blue were chosen to resemble the males' blue throat and abdominal patches; colour and luminance contrasts against the background were computed with a receptor-noise model using the collared lizard's cone sensitivities as a proxy because Sceloporus values are unavailable, and luminance contrast was highest for light blue, then grey, red, dark blue. Nulls: red v light blue FID was only near-significant (p = 0.082, d = 0.68); site (human activity) had no effect on FID (F = 1.51, p = 0.222); the colour x site interaction was not significant (p = 0.927). Capture probability also varied with colour (chi2 = 8.32, p = 0.040; 84 % with dark blue, nearly half that with grey or red). The shirts differ in more than hue, and one approaching person is the stimulus; a fear response to a coloured shirt, not a threshold, acuity or colour-discrimination measure.
quote: After correcting for multiple comparisons, we found that lizards fled at longer distances when approached with red compared to dark blue (Fig 1), a difference with a large effect (p = 0.033, Cohen’s d = 0.83).
note: Sentence read in pieces joined at 'distances' | 'when approached' and 'dark blue' | 'a difference'; the printed '(Fig 1),' was confirmed in a second pass. value: in a Y-maze with a food cue in one arm, 12 % of snails in acidified seawater (pH 7.6) chose the food side against 67 % in control seawater (pH 8.1) in the 2021 10-min set (Fisher's exact test p < 0.001)
units: categorical (% of snails choosing the food-cue arm, Fisher's exact test)

source.authors: Maria Manz, Joshua Lord, Melissa Morales
source.title: Ocean Acidification Impedes Foraging Behavior in the Mud Snail Ilyanassa obsoleta
source.journal: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering 11(3): 623

method: behavioural: Y-maze choice test, water from a header tank carrying the food cue entering one fork and seawater of the same pH only entering the other; time-limited trials
conditions: Snails collected from the intertidal zone of Raritan Bay, Cliffwood Beach, New Jersey and used within two months of collection, held at about pH 8.1, 25 C, 25 ppt. Control seawater pH 8.1; acidified pH 7.6 made by bubbling 1200 ppm CO2 air into a 12 L tank. The sentence is the first 2021 set (33 control and 33 acidified snails, 10 min limit, Hikari sinking carnivore pellets of fish and krill as the cue; Figure 2 caption sample sizes). Other sets: 2017 (20 and 20 snails, 20 min, crushed mussel Geukensia demissa) acidified snails were less successful but the difference was non-significant (Fisher p > 0.05); second 2021 set (16 control, 26 acidified, 5 min) food choice 50 v 16 %, empty-arm choice 0 v 42 %, p = 0.002; no-decision snails were recorded (21 % control, 55 % acidified in the 10 min set). The Methods do not say whether the food arm was randomised or alternated, whether snails were starved, whether each snail was tested once, or give sex or size; sets differed in maze shape, time limit, food and researcher. Percentages quoted for pooled results differ between Results and Discussion (control 84 v 87 or 88 %, acidified 27 v 36 %), so only the single-set sentence is used. Attraction of snails to a food odour in control water; the empty-arm share for the 10 min set is not given in the sentence, and there is no threshold or non-detection disclosure.
quote: In the second experiment (2021, 10 min time limit), snails in the acidified treatment were more than five times less likely to successfully choose the food side of the Y-maze (12%) than in the control treatments (67% success).
note: Sentence read in two abutting pieces ('more than five times' | 'less likely') with start and end seen; the Results call it 'the second experiment' while the Methods call it the first set in 2021 (the 2017 set being the first experiment overall).
